A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–D. Textual and visual inspection supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original synthetic experiments, Superconductivity and MNIST evaluations, kernel ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the work's original compression experiments, classification evaluations, kernel ablations, and runtime results.

M1.justification: Appendix B.11 newly specifies diagonal-subtraction terms for accelerated JKIP and ACKIP response updates with nonstationary kernels. The principal objectives and Algorithms 1–8 otherwise remain unchanged; these additions do not establish changes to the evaluated implementations.

E1.justification: The regression and classification tasks are retained, but Section 5.2.1 changes the Heteroscedastic input marginal from N(0, 3²) to N(0, 2²) while retaining identical plots. The PDFs do not establish whether the represented data population changed or only its description was corrected.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain JKH, JKIP, ACKH, ACKIP, random sampling, and the full-data reference where applicable. The revised discussion of Kernel Thinning does not change the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 5.2.1 revises the reported Heteroscedastic marginal variance from 9 to 4. This is a stated setting change without evidence of rerunning experiments. The evaluation metrics, splits, sample counts, optimization settings, and compressed-set sizes are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: The inverse-multiquadratic kernel ablation in Figures 20–21, compressed-set and decision-boundary examples, timing analysis, and AMCMD weighting examples in Figures 31–32 are retained without changed evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the reported 20 method runs, 500 random-sampling runs, medians with 25th–75th percentiles, boxplot conventions, and Table 1's means and standard deviations.

E6.justification: All 32 figure images and the timing-table values are unchanged, as are the reported performance rankings and qualitative findings. For example, Table 1 retains JKIP at 0.84 ± 0.081 seconds and ACKIP at 11.42 ± 0.04 seconds.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix B.2 add the constant kernel-feature norm assumption and restore the omitted diagonal term in the JKH derivation. Appendix B.6 restores 1/q normalization and corrects the empirical-average derivation; C.3.1 corrects the integration measure. B.11 adds nonstationary-kernel corrections, although the new JKIP coefficient 1/m is inconsistent with the 1/m² scaling in Equations 30–31.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about AMCMD, linear-time conditional compression, direct conditional targeting, and the advantages of joint optimization over greedy herding.

C2.justification: The revision explicitly qualifies JKH's kernel applicability and explains the need for diagonal corrections with nonstationary response kernels. Appendix A.1.1 also replaces Kernel Thinning's reported empirical inferiority with an explanation emphasizing information lost through discarded points.

D1.justification: Appendix B.11 adds concrete diagonal-handling instructions and corrects the full-data response vector from L_m to L_n in Equation 32. Hardware, software versions, optimizer and cross-validation details, pseudocode, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1.1 revises the critique of Kernel Thinning and clarifies how the conditional methods inherit herding and gradient-flow optimization approaches. The unique cited works are retained; reference reordering and removal of a duplicate Gentle entry are bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: Local passages explaining empirical objectives and classification probabilities are rewritten, an introductory motivation passage is moved, and transpose and gradient notation are standardized. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves above Figure 22, and local equation, caption, and page spacing changes occur. The figure images, table structures, and overall document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The added JKH assumption and diagonal term, together with the corrected AMCMD estimator proof, resolve concrete gaps in the justification of retained central results. These provide a limited improvement in rigor and clarity. The new nonstationary JKIP correction has an inconsistent coefficient, tempering the benefit, but this concerns an unevaluated extension rather than the constant-diagonal kernels used in the unchanged experiments.
